title.zh: 卷十 本紀第十: 肅宗
title.raw: 卷十 本紀第十: 肅宗 Volume 10 Annals 10: Suzong

sentences.zh: 肅宗文明武德大聖大宣孝皇帝諱亨，玄宗第三子，母曰元獻皇后楊氏。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong, posthumous title Civil Bright Martial Virtue Great Sage Great Proclaim Filial, bore the taboo name Heng, third son of Xuanzong; his mother was Empress Yuanxian of the Yang clan.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong — styled Civil Bright Martial Virtue Great Sage Great Proclaim Filial, bore the taboo name Heng. He was Xuanzong's third son; his mother was Empress Yuanxian of the Yang clan.

sentences.zh: 景雲二年乙亥生。

translations.literal: Born in Jingyun 2, yihai year.
translations.idiomatic: He was born in the yihai year of Jingyun 2.

sentences.zh: 初名嗣升，二歲封陜王，五歲拜安西大都護、河西四鎮諸蕃落大使。

translations.literal: Originally named Sisheng; at two he was enfeoffed Prince of Shan, at five appointed Grand Protector of Anxi and ambassador to the four western garrisons and various barbarian tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Originally named Sisheng, he was made Prince of Shan at two and at five became grand protector of Anxi and ambassador to the four western garrisons and border tribes.

sentences.zh: 上仁愛英悟，得之天然；

translations.literal: The prince was benevolent, intelligent, and perceptive by nature;
translations.idiomatic: He was benevolent and bright by nature;

sentences.zh: 及長，聰敏強記，屬辭典麗，耳目之所聽覽，不復遺忘。

translations.literal: when grown, keen and with strong memory, his compositions elegant; what his eyes and ears took in he never forgot.
translations.idiomatic: grown up, he was quick-witted and retentive, wrote elegant prose, and never forgot what he heard or saw.

sentences.zh: 開元十五年正月，封忠王，改名浚。

translations.literal: In the first month of Kaiyuan 15, he was enfeoffed Prince of Zhong and his name changed to Jun.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Kaiyuan 15 he was enfeoffed Prince of Zhong and renamed Jun.

sentences.zh: 五月，領朔方大使、單于大都護。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he took the posts of envoy of Shuofang and grand protector of Chanyu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he took command of Shuofang and became grand protector of Chanyu.

sentences.zh: 十八年，奚、契丹犯塞，以上為河北道元帥，信安王禕為副，帥御史大夫李朝隱、京兆尹裴伷先等八總管兵以討之。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year the Xi and Khitan raided the frontier; the prince was made commander-in-chief of Hebei circuit, Prince Xin'an Yi as deputy, leading Censor-in-Chief Li Chaoyin, metropolitan prefect Pei Youxian, and eight circuit generals to attack.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 18 the Xi and Khitan raided the frontier. He was made Hebei commander with Prince Xin'an Yi as deputy, leading Li Chaoyin, Pei Youxian, and eight circuit generals against them.

sentences.zh: 仍命百僚設次於光順門，與上相見。

translations.literal: Officials were also ordered to set pavilions at Guangshun Gate to meet the prince.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials were ordered to receive him at Guangshun Gate.

sentences.zh: 左丞相張說退謂學士孫逖、韋述曰：「嘗見太宗寫真圖，忠王英姿穎發，儀表非常，雅類聖祖，此社稷之福也。

translations.literal: Left Chancellor Zhang Yue, retiring, said to academicians Sun Ti and Wei Shu: "I have seen Taizong's portrait; Prince Zhong's heroic bearing and bright hair, his mien extraordinary—he greatly resembles the sage founder. This is the fortune of the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Left Chancellor Zhang Yue told academicians Sun Ti and Wei Shu: "I have seen Taizong's portrait. Prince Zhong's bearing and mien are extraordinary and greatly resemble our founding emperor. This is fortune for the realm.

sentences.zh: 」二十年，諸將大破奚、契丹，以上遙統之功，加司徒。

translations.literal: " In the twentieth year the generals crushed the Xi and Khitan; for the prince's remote command he was advanced to Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 20 the generals crushed the Xi and Khitan; for his overarching command he was made minister of education.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，改名璵。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year his name was changed to Yu.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 23 he was renamed Yu.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，皇太子瑛得罪。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year Crown Prince Ying fell from favor.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 25 Crown Prince Ying fell from favor.

sentences.zh: 二十六年六月庚子，立上為皇太子，改名紹。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the twenty-sixth year, on gengzi, the prince was installed as crown prince and his name changed to Shao.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi of the sixth month of Kaiyuan 26 he was made crown prince and renamed Shao.

sentences.zh: 後有言事者云：紹與宋太子名同，改今名。

translations.literal: Later a memorialist said Shao was the same name as a Song crown prince; he received his present name.
translations.idiomatic: Later a memorialist noted that Shao duplicated a Song crown prince's name; he took his present name accordingly.

sentences.zh: 初，太子瑛得罪，上召李林甫議立儲貳，時壽王瑁母武惠妃方承恩寵，林甫希旨，以瑁對。

translations.literal: At first, when Crown Prince Ying fell from favor, the emperor summoned Li Linfu to discuss establishing the heir; Consort Wu the Huifei, Prince Shou Mao's mother, then enjoyed favor, and Linfu to please her answered with Mao.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Ying fell, Xuanzong asked Li Linfu about the succession. Consort Wu Huifei, mother of Prince Shou Mao, then held favor, and Linfu named Mao to please her.

sentences.zh: 及立上為太子，林甫懼不利己，乃起韋堅、柳勣之獄，上幾危者數四。

translations.literal: When the prince was made crown prince, Linfu feared harm to himself and raised the cases of Wei Jian and Liu Ji; the prince was several times nearly endangered.
translations.idiomatic: After the prince's investiture Linfu feared for himself and framed Wei Jian and Liu Ji; the heir was nearly ruined four times.

sentences.zh: 後又楊國忠依倚妃家，恣為褻穢，懼上英武，潛謀不利，為患久之。

translations.literal: Later Yang Guozhong relied on the consort's clan, wantonly behaved obscenely, feared the prince's martial brilliance, and secretly plotted harm—a long menace.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yang Guozhong, leaning on the consort's kin, grew licentious and, fearing the prince's vigor, plotted against him for years.

sentences.zh: 天寶十三載正月，安祿山來朝，上嘗密奏，雲祿山有反相。

translations.literal: In the first month of Tianbao 13, An Lushan came to court; the prince secretly memorialized that Lushan had the aspect of rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Tianbao 13 An Lushan came to court, and the prince secretly reported that he bore the look of a rebel.

sentences.zh: 玄宗不聽。

translations.literal: Xuanzong would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong refused to heed him.

sentences.zh: 十四載十一月，祿山果叛，稱兵詣闕。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the fourteenth year Lushan indeed rebelled, raising troops toward the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Tianbao 14 Lushan rebelled and marched on the capital.

sentences.zh: 十二月丁未，陷東京。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on dingwei, the eastern capital fell.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei of the twelfth month the eastern capital fell.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，制太子監國，仍遣上親總諸軍進討。

translations.literal: On xinchou an edict had the crown prince oversee the state, and also sent the prince to personally command all armies to advance and attack.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou the court ordered the crown prince to oversee the realm and sent him to command the armies in person.

sentences.zh: 時祿山以誅楊國忠為名，由是軍民切齒於楊氏。

translations.literal: Then Lushan took executing Yang Guozhong as his pretext, and thus soldiers and people gritted their teeth at the Yang clan.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan marched under the banner of killing Yang Guozhong, and soldiers and civilians alike hated the Yangs.

sentences.zh: 國忠懼，乃與貴妃謀間其事，上遂不行。

translations.literal: Guozhong feared and with the Noble Consort plotted to obstruct the affair; the prince therefore did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong, afraid, colluded with the Noble Consort to block the campaign, and the prince never marched.

sentences.zh: 乃召河西節度使哥舒翰為皇太子前鋒兵馬元帥，令率眾二十萬守潼關。

translations.literal: Hexi military commissioner Ge Shuhan was summoned as the crown prince's vanguard commander and ordered to lead two hundred thousand to hold Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Shuhan of Hexi was made the crown prince's vanguard commander with two hundred thousand men to hold Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 至德一載明年六月，哥舒翰為賊所敗，關門不守，國忠諷玄宗幸蜀。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the next year after Zhide 1, Ge Shuhan was defeated by the rebels, the pass could not be held, and Guozhong urged Xuanzong to go to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Zhide 2 Ge Shuhan was routed, Tong Pass fell, and Guozhong urged flight to Shu.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，至馬嵬頓，六軍不進，請誅楊氏。

translations.literal: On dingyou they reached Mawei halt; the six armies would not advance and demanded execution of the Yang clan.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou at Mawei the army halted and demanded the Yangs' deaths.

sentences.zh: 於是誅國忠，賜貴妃自盡。

translations.literal: Guozhong was executed and the Noble Consort ordered to take her own life.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong was killed and the Noble Consort ordered to die by her own hand.

sentences.zh: 車駕將發，留上在後宣諭百姓。

translations.literal: As the imperial carriage was about to depart, the prince was left behind to proclaim reassurance to the people.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor prepared to flee, the prince remained to reassure the people.

sentences.zh: 眾泣而言曰：「逆胡背恩，主上播越，臣等生於聖代，世為唐民，願戮力一心，為國討賊，請從太子收復長安。

translations.literal: The crowd wept and said: "The rebel barbarian has betrayed grace; the sovereign is cast adrift. We were born in this sagely age and are Tang subjects through generations; we wish to join as one to punish the rebel for the state—let us follow the crown prince to recover Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: The crowd wept: "The rebel has betrayed the throne. We are Tang subjects of a golden age and beg to follow the crown prince to recover Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 」玄宗聞之曰：「此天啟也。

translations.literal: " Xuanzong heard and said: "This is Heaven's opening.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong heard them and said: "Heaven has spoken.

sentences.zh: 」乃令高力士與壽王瑁送太子內人及服御等物，留後軍廄馬從上。

translations.literal: " He ordered Gao Lishi and Prince Shou Mao to send the crown prince's inner attendants and robes and gear, leaving rear stable horses to follow the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Gao Lishi and Prince Shou Mao with the prince's household and gear, keeping the rear stable horses for himself.

sentences.zh: 令力士口宣曰：「汝好去！

translations.literal: Lishi was ordered to proclaim: "Go well!
translations.idiomatic: Lishi proclaimed: "Go in peace!

sentences.zh: 百姓屬望，慎勿違之。

translations.literal: The people look to you; take care not to disappoint them.
translations.idiomatic: The people look to you—do not fail them.

sentences.zh: 莫以吾為意。

translations.literal: Do not mind me."
translations.idiomatic: Think nothing of me."

sentences.zh: 且西戎北狄，吾嘗厚之，今國步艱難，必得其用，汝其勉之！

translations.literal: Moreover the western and northern barbarians—I have always treated them generously; now the state is in hardship and will surely need their service. Strive onward!"
translations.idiomatic: I have always treated the western and northern peoples well; in this crisis they will serve you. Press on!"

sentences.zh: 」上回至渭北，便橋已斷，水暴漲，無舟楫；

translations.literal: " The prince returned to north of the Wei; Bian Bridge was broken, the waters swelled, there were no boats;
translations.idiomatic: North of the Wei he found Bian Bridge broken and the river in flood, with no boats;

sentences.zh: 上號令水濱百姓，歸者三千餘人。

translations.literal: the prince ordered the riverside people; more than three thousand returned.
translations.idiomatic: he rallied the riverside people and gathered more than three thousand.

sentences.zh: 渭水可涉，又遇潼關散卒，誤以為賊，與之戰，士眾多傷。

translations.literal: The Wei could be waded; they also met scattered soldiers from Tong Pass, mistook them for rebels, fought, and many were wounded.
translations.idiomatic: They forded the Wei, mistook scattered Tong Pass troops for rebels, and many were wounded in the fight.

sentences.zh: 乃收其餘眾北上，軍既濟，其後皆溺，上喜，以為天之佑。

translations.literal: Gathering the remainder he went north; once the army crossed, those behind all drowned; the prince rejoiced, taking it as Heaven's aid.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered the survivors and crossed north; those behind drowned, and he took it as Heaven's blessing.

sentences.zh: 時從上惟廣平、建寧二王及四軍將士，才二千人。

translations.literal: Then those with the prince were only Princes Guangping and Jianning and four-army officers and soldiers—only two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Only Princes Guangping and Jianning and two thousand troops from four armies remained with him.

sentences.zh: 自奉天而北，夕次永壽，百姓遮道獻牛酒。

translations.literal: From Fengtian northward, they halted at night at Yongshou; the people blocked the road offering cattle and wine.
translations.idiomatic: From Fengtian northward they rested at Yongshou, where people brought cattle and wine.

sentences.zh: 有白雲起西北，長數丈，如樓閣之狀，議者以為天子之氣。

translations.literal: White clouds rose from the northwest, several zhang long, like towers; commentators took it for the qi of the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: White clouds rose from the northwest like towers; men called it the emperor's omen.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，至新平郡。

translations.literal: On wuxu he reached Xinping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu he came to Xinping commandery.

sentences.zh: 時晝夜奔馳三百餘里，士眾器械亡失過半，所存之眾，不過一旅。

translations.literal: Day and night they galloped more than three hundred li; troops and equipment lost more than half; those remaining were barely one brigade.
translations.idiomatic: They rode day and night three hundred li; half the men and gear were gone, barely a brigade left.

sentences.zh: 己亥，至安定郡，斬新平太守薛羽、保定太守徐㲄，以其棄郡也。

translations.literal: On jihai he reached Anding commandery and executed Xinping prefect Xue Yu and Baoding prefect Xu She, for abandoning their commands.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai at Anding he executed the prefects of Xinping and Baoding for abandoning their posts.

sentences.zh: 庚子，至烏氏驛，彭原太守李遵謁見，率兵士奉迎，仍進衣服糧糗。

translations.literal: On gengzi he reached Wushi post; Pengyuan prefect Li Zun came to meet, leading soldiers to welcome and advancing clothes and grain.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi at Wushi post Pengyuan prefect Li Zun came with troops, clothing, and grain.

sentences.zh: 上至彭原，又募得甲士四百，率私馬以助軍。

translations.literal: At Pengyuan the prince also recruited four hundred armored soldiers, leading private horses to aid the army.
translations.idiomatic: At Pengyuan he raised four hundred more armored men and private horses for the army.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，至平涼郡，蒐閱監牧公私馬，得數萬疋，官軍益振。

translations.literal: On xinchou he reached Pingliang commandery, mustered public and private horses of the pastures, obtained tens of thousands, and the official army grew stronger.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou at Pingliang he gathered tens of thousands of pasture horses and the army grew strong.

sentences.zh: 時賊據長安，知上治兵河西。

translations.literal: The rebels held Chang'an and knew the prince was training troops in Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels in Chang'an learned he was gathering forces in Hexi.

sentences.zh: 三輔百姓皆曰：「吾太子大軍即至！

translations.literal: The people of the Three Adjuncts all said: "Our crown prince's great army is coming!
translations.idiomatic: People of the capital region cried: "The crown prince's army comes!

sentences.zh: 」賊望西北塵起，有時奔走。

translations.literal: " The rebels seeing dust rise in the northwest sometimes fled.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing dust in the northwest, the rebels sometimes fled.

sentences.zh: 戊申，扶風人康景龍殺賊宣慰使薛總等二百餘人，陳倉令薛景仙率眾收扶風郡守之。

translations.literal: On wushen Fufeng man Kang Jinglong killed more than two hundred of the rebels' pacification commissioners including Xue Zong; Chencang magistrate Xue Jingxian led troops to recover and hold Fufeng commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen Kang Jinglong of Fufeng killed two hundred rebel commissioners; Xue Jingxian of Chencang recovered Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 由是關輔豪右皆謀殺賊，賊故不敢侵軼。

translations.literal: Hence the great families of Guanfu all plotted to kill rebels, and the rebels therefore dared not raid.
translations.idiomatic: Guanfu gentry then plotted against the rebels, who dared not raid.

sentences.zh: 上在平涼，數日之間未知所適，會朔方留後杜鴻漸、魏少游、崔漪等遣判官李涵奉箋迎上，備陳兵馬招集之勢，倉儲庫甲之數，上大悅。

translations.literal: At Pingliang, for several days the prince did not know where to go; Shuofang acting commissioner Du Hongjian, Wei Shaoyou, Cui Yi and others sent judge Li Han with a letter welcoming the prince, fully describing gathered troops and stores of grain and armor; the prince was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: At Pingliang he still did not know his course when Du Hongjian, Wei Shaoyou, and Cui Yi of Shuofang sent Li Han to welcome him with reports of troops, stores, and armor. He rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 鴻漸又發朔方步騎數千人於白草頓奉迎。

translations.literal: Hongjian also dispatched several thousand Shuofang infantry and cavalry to Baicao halt to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Hongjian sent several thousand Shuofang horsemen to meet him at Baicao.

sentences.zh: 時河西行軍司馬裴冕新授御史中丞赴闕，遇上於平涼，亦勸上治兵於靈武以圖進取，上然之。

translations.literal: Hexi campaigning marshal Pei Mian, newly appointed censor and heading to court, met the prince at Pingliang and also urged him to train troops at Lingwu for advance; the prince agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Mian of Hexi, newly made censor en route to court, met him at Pingliang and urged gathering an army at Lingwu; he agreed.

sentences.zh: 上初發平涼，有彩雲浮空，白鶴前引，出軍之後，有黃龍自上所憩屋騰空而去。

translations.literal: When the prince first left Pingliang, colored clouds floated in the sky, a white crane led ahead; after the army departed, a yellow dragon rose from the house where he had rested and flew into the sky.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving Pingliang he saw auspicious clouds, a white crane leading the way, and a yellow dragon rising from his resting place.

sentences.zh: 上行至豐寧南，見黃河天塹之固，欲整軍北渡，以保豐寧，忽大風飛沙，跬步之間，不辨人物，及回軍趨靈武，風沙頓止，天地廓清。

translations.literal: Going south of Fengning he saw the Yellow River's natural barrier, wished to cross north to hold Fengning; suddenly great wind and flying sand—in a few steps one could not distinguish people; when the army turned toward Lingwu the wind and sand stopped at once and heaven and earth cleared.
translations.idiomatic: South of Fengning he meant to cross the Yellow River and hold Fengning, but sandstorms blinded the march; turning toward Lingwu the sky cleared.

sentences.zh: 七月辛酉，上至靈武，時魏少游預備供帳，無不畢備。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, on xinyou, the prince reached Lingwu; Wei Shaoyou had prepared provisions and pavilions, all complete.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou of the seventh month he reached Lingwu, where Wei Shaoyou had everything ready.

sentences.zh: 裴冕、杜鴻漸等從容進曰：「今寇逆亂常，毒流函谷，主上倦勤大位，移幸蜀川。

translations.literal: Pei Mian, Du Hongjian and others calmly advanced, saying: "Now the rebel violates the norm, poison flows to Hangu; the sovereign wearies of the throne and has moved to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Mian and Du Hongjian said calmly: "Rebels poison the realm; the emperor has fled to Shu.

sentences.zh: 江山阻險，奏請路絕，宗社神器，須有所歸。

translations.literal: Rivers and mountains block the way, memorials cannot reach; the altars and sacred vessel must have a master."
translations.idiomatic: Roads are cut and the throne cannot stand empty."

sentences.zh: 萬姓顒顒，思崇明聖，天意人事，不可固違。

translations.literal: The myriad people look up, thinking to exalt the sage lord; Heaven's will and human affairs cannot be stubbornly resisted.
translations.idiomatic: The people look to a sage ruler; heaven and earth cannot wait."

sentences.zh: 伏願殿下順其樂推，以安社稷，王者之大孝也。

translations.literal: We humbly wish Your Highness follow their willing acclaim to settle the altars—the great filiality of a true king."
translations.idiomatic: We beg Your Highness accept their acclaim and secure the altars—the greatest filial piety."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「俟平寇逆，奉迎鑾輿，從容儲闈，侍膳左右，豈不樂哉！

translations.literal: " The prince said: "Wait until the rebels are pacified, welcome back the imperial carriage, calmly in the eastern palace, attending at meals—would that not be joy!
translations.idiomatic: He said: "When the rebels are beaten I will welcome the emperor home and serve in the eastern palace—what could be happier!

sentences.zh: 公等何急也？

translations.literal: Why are you so urgent?"
translations.idiomatic: Why such haste?"

sentences.zh: 」冕等凡六上箋。

translations.literal: " Mian and the others memorialized six times in all.
translations.idiomatic: Mian and the others memorialized six times.

sentences.zh: 辭情激切，上不獲已，乃從。

translations.literal: Their words were urgent and impassioned; the prince could not refuse and assented.
translations.idiomatic: Their pleas were fierce; he could not refuse and assented.

sentences.zh: 是月甲子，上即皇帝位於靈武。

translations.literal: That month, on jiazi, the prince ascended the throne at Lingwu.
translations.idiomatic: That month, on jiazi, he took the throne at Lingwu.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，冕等跪進曰：「自逆賊恁陵，兩京失守，聖皇傳位陛下，再安區宇，臣稽首上千萬歲壽。

translations.literal: When rites were complete, Mian and others knelt and advanced: "Since the rebel defied heaven and the two capitals fell, the sage emperor has passed the throne to Your Majesty to re-settle the realm—we bow and wish ten thousand years."
translations.idiomatic: When rites ended Mian knelt: "The rebel seized the capitals; the retired emperor passed you the throne. We bow and wish you ten thousand years."

sentences.zh: 」群臣舞蹈稱萬歲。

translations.literal: " The ministers danced and shouted ten thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers shouted ten thousand years.

sentences.zh: 上流涕歔欷，感動左右。

translations.literal: The emperor wept and sobbed, moving those around him.
translations.idiomatic: He wept, moving all around him.

sentences.zh: 即日奏其事於上皇。

translations.literal: That day he reported the matter to the Retired Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: That day he reported to the retired emperor.

sentences.zh: 是日，御靈武南門，下制曰：

translations.literal: That day he held court at Lingwu's south gate and issued an edict:
translations.idiomatic: That day at Lingwu's south gate he issued an edict:

sentences.zh: 以朔方度支副使、大理司直杜鴻漸為兵部郎中，朔方節度判官崔漪為吏部郎中，並知中書舍人。

translations.literal: Shuofang revenue vice commissioner and directorate of justice clerk Du Hongjian was made Director of the Ministry of War; Shuofang circuit judge Cui Yi was made Director of the Ministry of Personnel, both acting as drafting secretaries.
translations.idiomatic: Du Hongjian became director of war and Cui Yi director of personnel, both acting drafting secretaries.

sentences.zh: 以御史中丞裴冕為中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Pei Mian was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and concurrent Secretariat-Chancellery Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Mian became vice director of the secretariat and grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 河西兵馬使周佖為河西節度使，隴右兵馬使彭元暉為隴右節度使，前蒲州刺史呂崇賁為關內節度使兼順化郡太守。

translations.literal: Hexi army commissioner Zhou Yi was made Hexi military commissioner; Longyou army commissioner Peng Yuanhui was made Longyou military commissioner; former Pu prefect Lü Chongben was made Guannei military commissioner and concurrent Shunhua prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yi became Hexi commissioner, Peng Yuanhui Longyou commissioner, and Lü Chongben Guannei commissioner and Shunhua prefect.

sentences.zh: 以陳倉縣令薛景仙為扶風太守，以隴右節度使郭英乂為天水郡太守。

translations.literal: Chencang magistrate Xue Jingxian was made Fufeng prefect; Longyou military commissioner Guo Yingyi was made Tianshui prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Jingxian became Fufeng prefect and Guo Yingyi Tianshui prefect.

sentences.zh: 改靈武郡為大都督府，上縣為望，中縣為上。

translations.literal: Lingwu commandery was changed to a great protectorate prefecture; upper counties became wang and middle counties shang.
translations.idiomatic: Lingwu became a great protectorate; upper counties were raised to wang and middle to shang.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，逆胡害霍國長公主、永王妃侯莫陳氏、義王妃閻氏、陳王妃韋氏、信王妃任氏、駙馬楊朏等八十餘人於崇仁之街。

translations.literal: On dingmao the rebels killed Princess Huoguo the Long, Princess Yong the Consort Hou Mo, Princess Yi the Consort Yan, Princess Chen the Consort Wei, Princess Xin the Consort Ren, and Chief Son-in-Law Yang Fei and more than eighty others on Chongren Street.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao rebels killed Princess Huoguo, Princesses Yong, Yi, Chen, and Xin, Chief Son-in-Law Yang Fei, and more than eighty kin on Chongren Street.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，賊黨同羅部五千餘人自西京出降朔方軍。

translations.literal: On jiaxu more than five thousand of the rebel Tongluo band surrendered to the Shuofang army from the western capital.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu more than five thousand Tongluo rebels surrendered to Shuofang from the western capital.

sentences.zh: 己卯，京兆尹崔光遠、長安令蘇震等率府縣官吏大呼於西市，殺賊數千級，然後來赴行在。

translations.literal: On jimao metropolitan prefect Cui Guangyuan, Chang'an magistrate Su Zhen and others led district officials shouting at the western market, killing several thousand rebels, then came to the mobile court.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao Cui Guangyuan and Su Zhen of Chang'an led officials in the western market, killed thousands of rebels, and joined the court.

sentences.zh: 詔改扶風為鳳翔郡。

translations.literal: An edict changed Fufeng to Fengxiang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: An edict renamed Fufeng Fengxiang commandery.

sentences.zh: 八月壬午，朔方節度使郭子儀、范陽節度使李光弼破賊於常山郡之嘉山。

translations.literal: On renwu Shuofang military commissioner Guo Ziyi and Fanyang military commissioner Li Guangbi crushed the rebels at Jia Mountain in Changshan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu Guo Ziyi and Li Guangbi routed the rebels at Jia Mountain in Changshan.

sentences.zh: 上以治兵收京城，詔子儀等旋師，子儀、光弼率所統步騎五萬至自河北。

translations.literal: As the emperor trained troops to recover the capital, an edict ordered Ziyi and others to turn their armies; Ziyi and Guangbi led fifty thousand foot and horse from Hebei to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Training to retake the capital, he recalled Ziyi and Guangbi, who brought fifty thousand troops from Hebei.

sentences.zh: 詔以子儀為兵部尚書，依前靈州大都督府長史；

translations.literal: An edict made Ziyi Minister of War, still chief of the Lingzhou great protectorate;
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi was made minister of war and still chief of Lingzhou protectorate;

sentences.zh: 光弼為戶部尚書，兼太原尹、北京留守：同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Guangbi Minister of Revenue, concurrent Taiyuan prefect and northern capital guardian: both concurrent Secretariat-Chancellery Grand Councilors.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi minister of revenue, Taiyuan prefect, and northern capital guardian—both grand councilors.

sentences.zh: 回紇、吐蕃遣使繼至，請和親，願助國討賊，皆宴賜遣之。

translations.literal: Huihe and Tibet sent envoys in succession, seeking marriage alliance and wishing to aid the state in punishing rebels—all were feasted and rewarded and sent off.
translations.idiomatic: Huihe and Tibet sent envoys offering alliance and troops against the rebels; all were feasted and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 是日，上皇至成都，大赦。

translations.literal: That day the Retired Emperor reached Chengdu and proclaimed a great amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: That day Xuanzong reached Chengdu and amnestied the realm.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，上所奉表始達成都。

translations.literal: On guisi the emperor's memorial first reached Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi his memorial reached Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，上皇遜位稱誥，遣左相韋見素、文部尚書房琯、門下侍郎崔渙等奉冊書赴靈武。

translations.literal: On dingyou the Retired Emperor abdicated as proclamation sovereign and sent Left Chancellor Wei Jiansu, Minister of Culture Fang Guan, and Vice Director of the Chancellery Cui Huan with investiture documents to Lingwu.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou the retired emperor abdicated and sent Wei Jiansu, Fang Guan, and Cui Huan to Lingwu with the investiture.

sentences.zh: 九月戊辰，上南幸彭原郡。

translations.literal: On wuchen the emperor went south to Pengyuan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen he went south to Pengyuan.

sentences.zh: 封故邠王守禮男承寀為燉煌王，令使回紇和親，冊回紇可汗女為毗伽公主，仍令僕固懷恩送承寀至回紇部。

translations.literal: The former Prince of Bin Shouli's son Chengbao was enfeoffed Prince of Dunhuang and sent to Huihe for marriage; the Huihe qaghan's daughter was invested Princess Pijia, and Pugu Huai'en was ordered to escort Chengbao to the Huihe tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Chengbao was made Prince of Dunhuang for a Huihe marriage; the qaghan's daughter became Princess Pijia, and Pugu Huai'en escorted him.

sentences.zh: 內官邊令誠背上皇投賊，至是復來見，上命斬之。

translations.literal: Inner attendant Bian Lingcheng had turned the Retired Emperor over to the rebels and now came again; the emperor ordered him executed.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Lingcheng, who had delivered the retired emperor to the rebels, returned and was executed.

sentences.zh: 丙子，至順化郡，韋見素、房琯、崔渙等自蜀郡賚上冊書及傳國寶等至。

translations.literal: On bingzi he reached Shunhua commandery; Wei Jiansu, Fang Guan, Cui Huan and others from Shu commandery brought the investiture documents and the imperial seal.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi at Shunhua, Wei Jiansu, Fang Guan, and Cui Huan arrived from Shu with the seal and investiture.

sentences.zh: 己卯，斬潼關敗將李承光於纛下。

translations.literal: On jimao the Tong Pass defeated general Li Chengguang was beheaded below the banners.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao Li Chengguang, defeated at Tong Pass, was beheaded before the army.

sentences.zh: 十月辛巳朔，日有蝕之，既。

translations.literal: On xinsi, the first day of the tenth month, the sun was eclipsed to totality.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi, the tenth month's new moon, the sun was eclipsed to totality.

sentences.zh: 癸未，彭原郡以軍興用度不足，權賣官爵及度僧尼。

translations.literal: On guisi Pengyuan commandery, for lack of military funds, temporarily sold offices and ranks and licensed monks and nuns.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi Pengyuan, short of war funds, sold offices and licensed monks and nuns.

sentences.zh: 上素知房琯名，至是琯請為兵馬元帥收復兩京，許之，仍令兵部尚書王思禮為副。

translations.literal: The emperor had long known Fang Guan's name; now Guan requested to be commander to recover the two capitals and was permitted, with Minister of War Wang Sili still as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Fang Guan's reputation, he made him commander to retake the two capitals with Wang Sili as deputy.

sentences.zh: 分兵為三軍，楊希文、劉貴哲、李光進等各將一軍，其眾五萬。

translations.literal: The army was divided into three corps; Yang Xiwen, Liu Guizhe, and Li Guangjin each commanded one corps, their forces fifty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He split the army into three corps under Yang Xiwen, Liu Guizhe, and Li Guangjin—fifty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，琯與賊將安守忠戰於陳濤斜，官軍敗績，楊希文、劉貴哲等降於賊，琯亦奔還。

translations.literal: On xinchou Guan fought the rebel general An Shouzhong at Chen-Tao Slope; the official army was defeated, Yang Xiwen, Liu Guizhe and others surrendered to the rebels, and Guan also fled back.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou Fang Guan met An Shouzhong at Chen-Tao Slope, was routed, and lost Yang Xiwen and Liu Guizhe to surrender.

sentences.zh: 平原太守顏真卿以食盡援絕，棄城渡河，於是河北郡縣盡陷於賊。

translations.literal: Pingyuan prefect Yan Zhenqing, food exhausted and relief cut off, abandoned the city and crossed the river; then all Hebei commanderies fell to the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhenqing of Pingyuan, starving and cut off, fled across the river; Hebei then fell to the rebels.

sentences.zh: 十一月辛亥，河西地震有聲，圮裂廬舍，張掖、酒泉尤甚。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on xinhai, Hexi suffered an earthquake with sound; houses collapsed and split, Zhangye and Jiuquan worst.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Hexi shook with a roaring earthquake; Zhangye and Jiuquan suffered worst.

sentences.zh: 戊子，回紇引軍來赴難，與郭子儀同破賊黨同羅部三千餘眾於河上。

translations.literal: On wuzi Huihe led troops to aid the cause and with Guo Ziyi together crushed more than three thousand of the rebel Tongluo band on the river.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi Huihe came to aid and with Guo Ziyi destroyed three thousand Tongluo rebels on the river.

sentences.zh: 詔宰相崔渙巡撫江南，補授官吏。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Chancellor Cui Huan to tour and pacify Jiangnan, appointing and confirming officials.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Huan was sent to tour Jiangnan and appoint officials.

sentences.zh: 十二月戊子，以王思禮為關內節度。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on wuzi, Wang Sili was made Guannei military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Wang Sili became Guannei commissioner.

sentences.zh: 彭原郡百姓給復二載，郡同六雄，縣升緊、望。

translations.literal: Pengyuan commandery's people were given tax relief for two years; the commandery ranked with the six great circuits, its counties raised to jin and wang.
translations.idiomatic: Pengyuan received two years' tax relief, rank equal to the six great circuits, and its counties were raised.

sentences.zh: 以秦州都督郭英乂為鳳翔太守，諫議大夫高適為廣陵長史、淮南節度兼採訪使。

translations.literal: Qinzhou protector Guo Yingyi was made Fengxiang prefect; Remonstrance Grandee Gao Shi was made Guangling prefect and Huainan military commissioner and pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yingyi became Fengxiang prefect; Gao Shi became Guangling prefect and Huainan commissioner.

sentences.zh: 賊將阿史那承慶攻陷潁川郡，執太守薛願、長史龐堅。

translations.literal: The rebel general Ashina Chengqing took Yingchuan commandery and seized prefect Xue Yuan and chief clerk Pang Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Ashina Chengqing took Yingchuan and seized Xue Yuan and Pang Jian.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，江陵大都督府永王璘擅領舟師下廣陵。

translations.literal: On jiachen the Jiangling great protectorate's Prince of Yong Li Lin on his own led a fleet down to Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen Prince of Yong Li Lin led a fleet down to Guangling on his own authority.

sentences.zh: 至德二載二載春正月庚戌朔，上在彭原受朝賀。

translations.literal: Zhide 2 year, Zhide 2, first spring month, on gengxu new moon, the emperor at Pengyuan received New Year court.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Zhide 2, on gengxu, he received New Year court at Pengyuan.

sentences.zh: 是日通表入蜀賀上皇。

translations.literal: That day a memorial of felicitation was sent into Shu to congratulate the Retired Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: That day felicitation was sent to the retired emperor in Shu.

sentences.zh: 上皇在蜀，每得上表疏，訊其使者，知上涕戀晨省，乃下誥曰：「至和育物，大孝安親，古之哲王，必由斯道。

translations.literal: The Retired Emperor in Shu, whenever he received the emperor's memorials, questioned the messenger and learned the emperor's tearful longing for morning and evening attendance; he then issued a proclamation:
translations.idiomatic: In Shu the retired emperor, learning from each messenger of his son's tearful devotion, issued a proclamation:

sentences.zh: 朕往在春宮，嘗事先後，問安靡闕，視膳無違。

translations.literal: "Supreme harmony nurturing things, great filiality settling kin—the ancient sage kings surely walked this path.
translations.idiomatic: "Supreme harmony and great filial piety were the path of the sage kings of old.

sentences.zh: 及同氣天倫，聯華棣萼，居嘗共被，食必分甘。

translations.literal: I once served in the eastern palace, attending the empresses morning and evening without fail, sharing meals without preference.
translations.idiomatic: I once served my parents in the eastern palace without fail.

sentences.zh: 今皇帝奉而行之，未嘗失墜，每有銜命而來，戒途將發，必肅恭拜跪，涕泗漣洏，左右侍臣，罔不感動。

translations.literal: Now the emperor carries this out without lapse; whenever an envoy comes and is about to depart, he bows with solemn reverence, tears streaming, moving all attendants.
translations.idiomatic: My son has never failed in this; every envoy reports his tears and reverence, moving all who see.

sentences.zh: 間者抱戴、赤雀、白狼之瑞，接武薦臻，此皆皇帝聖敬之符，孝友之感也。

translations.literal: Lately auspicious signs—the holding infant, red sparrow, white wolf—have come in succession; all are marks of the emperor's sage reverence and filial feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Auspicious omens have followed one another—marks of his sage reverence and filial heart.

sentences.zh: 故能誕敷德教，橫於四海，信可以光宅寰宇，永綏黎元者哉！

translations.literal: Thus he spreads virtue across the four seas and may truly illuminate the realm and forever pacify the people!
translations.idiomatic: He spreads virtue across the seas and may truly pacify the realm forever!

sentences.zh: 其天下有至孝友悌行著鄉閭堪旌表者，郡縣長官採聽聞奏，庶孝子順孫沐於玄化也。

translations.literal: Let all under heaven who show supreme filial piety and brotherly harmony renowned in their villages be reported by county and prefecture magistrates, that filial sons and obedient grandsons may bathe in profound transformation."
translations.idiomatic: Let magistrates report filial sons and obedient grandsons throughout the realm."

sentences.zh: 」甲寅，以襄陽太守李峘為蜀郡長史、劍南節度使，將作少監魏仲犀為襄陽、山南道節度使，永王傅劉匯為丹陽太守兼防禦使。

translations.literal: On jiayin Xiangyang prefect Li Xian was made Shu prefect and Jiannan military commissioner; Master of Works Vice Director Wei Zhongxi was made Xiangyang and Shannandao military commissioner; Prince of Yong tutor Liu Hui was made Danyang prefect and concurrent defense commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin Li Xian became Shu prefect and Jiannan commissioner; Wei Zhongxi Xiangyang commissioner; Liu Hui Danyang prefect and defender.

sentences.zh: 以憲部尚書李麟同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Minister of Justice Li Lin was made concurrent Secretariat-Chancellery Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Li Lin, minister of justice, became grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 上皇遣平章事崔圓奉誥赴彭原。

translations.literal: The Retired Emperor sent Grand Councilor Cui Yuan with a proclamation to Pengyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The retired emperor sent Cui Yuan to Pengyuan with a proclamation.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，逆胡安祿山為其子慶緒所殺。

translations.literal: On yimao the rebel An Lushan was killed by his son Qingxu.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao An Lushan was killed by his son Qingxu.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，於江寧縣置金陵郡，仍置軍，分人以鎮之。

translations.literal: On xinyou Jinling commandery was established at Jiangning county, with an army posted and people divided to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou Jinling commandery was founded at Jiangning with a garrison.

sentences.zh: 甲子，幸保定郡。

translations.literal: On jiazi he went to Baoding commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi he went to Baoding.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，武威郡九姓商胡安門物等叛，殺節度使周佖，判官崔稱率眾討平之。

translations.literal: On bingyin merchants of the nine surnames in Wuwei commandery, An Menwu and others, rebelled, killed military commissioner Zhou Yi; judge Cui Cheng led troops and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin Nine-Surname merchants in Wuwei rebelled and killed Zhou Yi; Cui Cheng put them down.

sentences.zh: 是日，蜀郡健兒賈秀等五千人謀逆，上皇禦蜀郡南樓，將軍席元慶等討平之。

translations.literal: That day five thousand Shu braves under Jia Xiu plotted treason; the Retired Emperor mounted the south tower of Shu commandery; generals Xi Yuanqing and others suppressed them.
translations.idiomatic: That day five thousand Shu braves plotted treason; Xuanzong took the south tower while Xi Yuanqing suppressed them.

sentences.zh: 二月戊子，幸鳳翔郡。

translations.literal: In the second month, on wuzi, he went to Fengxiang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month he went to Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 文城太守武威郡九姓齊莊破賊五千餘眾。

translations.literal: Wencheng prefect Qi Zhuang of the nine surnames of Wuwei crushed more than five thousand rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Zhuang of Wencheng crushed five thousand rebels.

sentences.zh: 上議大舉收復兩京，盡括公私馬以助軍。

translations.literal: The emperor discussed a great campaign to recover the two capitals and requisitioned all public and private horses to aid the army.
translations.idiomatic: He planned a great drive on the two capitals and requisitioned every horse.

sentences.zh: 給事中李暠署云「無馬」，大夫崔光遠劾之，貶暠江華太守。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Li Hao submitted a note saying "no horses"; Censor-in-Chief Cui Guangyuan impeached him and Hao was demoted to Jianghua prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hao claimed "no horses"; Cui Guangyuan impeached him and he was demoted to Jianghua.

sentences.zh: 節度使李光弼大破賊將蔡希德之眾於城下，斬虜七萬，軍資器杖稱是。

translations.literal: Military commissioner Li Guangbi crushed the rebel general Cai Xide's host below the city wall, beheading and capturing seventy thousand; military stores and weapons were abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangbi routed Cai Xide below the walls, taking seventy thousand heads and rich spoils.

sentences.zh: 朔方節度使郭子儀大破賊將崔乾祐於潼關，收河東郡。

translations.literal: Shuofang military commissioner Guo Ziyi crushed the rebel general Cui Qianyou at Tong Pass and recovered Hedong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi routed Cui Qianyou at Tong Pass and recovered Hedong.

sentences.zh: 永王璘兵敗，奔於嶺外，至大庾嶺，為洪州刺史皇甫侁所殺。

translations.literal: Prince of Yong Li Lin's army was defeated; he fled beyond the ranges and at Dayu Ridge was killed by Hongzhou prefect Huangfu Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Li Lin was defeated, fled south, and was killed at Dayu by Huangfu Shen.

sentences.zh: 三月癸亥，河西自去冬地震，至是方止。

translations.literal: In the third month, on guihai, Hexi's earthquake since last winter now ceased.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Hexi's winter-long earthquake finally ceased.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，以左相韋見素、平章事裴冕為左右僕射，並罷知政事。

translations.literal: On xinyou Left Chancellor Wei Jiansu and Grand Councilor Pei Mian were made Left and Right Vice Directors of the Masters of Writing, both removed from deliberative posts.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou Wei Jiansu and Pei Mian became left and right vice directors of the masters of writing and left the council.

sentences.zh: 以前憲部尚書致仕苗晉卿為左相。

translations.literal: Former Minister of Justice, retired, Miao Jinqing was made Left Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Retired Minister of Justice Miao Jinqing became left chancellor.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃遣使和親，遣給事中南巨川報命。

translations.literal: Tibet sent envoys for marriage alliance; Palace Attendant Nan Juchuan was sent to reply.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet sought alliance; Nan Juchuan was sent to reply.

sentences.zh: 癸亥大雨，至癸酉不止，詔疏理刑獄，甲戌方止。

translations.literal: From guihai heavy rain fell until guiyou without stopping; an edict ordered review of criminal cases, and on jiaxu it ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy rain fell from guihai to guiyou; he ordered prisons reviewed, and on jiaxu the rains stopped.

sentences.zh: 夏四月戊寅朔，以郭子儀為司空，兼副元帥，統諸節度；

translations.literal: In the fourth summer month, on wuyin new moon, Guo Ziyi was made Minister of Works and concurrent deputy commander-in-chief, commanding all military commissioners;
translations.idiomatic: On the fourth month's new moon Guo Ziyi became minister of works and deputy commander, commanding all commissioners;

sentences.zh: 李光弼為司徒。

translations.literal: Li Guangbi was made Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangbi became minister of education.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，太史奏歲星、太白、熒惑集於東井。

translations.literal: On yiyou the imperial astronomer reported Jupiter, Venus, and Mars gathered in the Well mansion.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou the court astronomer reported Jupiter, Venus, and Mars in the Well mansion.

sentences.zh: 五月癸丑，郭子儀與賊將安守忠戰於清渠，官軍敗績，子儀退保武功。

translations.literal: On guichou Guo Ziyi fought the rebel general An Shouzhong at Qing Canal; the official army was defeated and Ziyi withdrew to defend Wugong.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou Guo Ziyi fought An Shouzhong at Qing Canal, was routed, and withdrew to Wugong.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，房琯為太子少師，罷知政事。

translations.literal: On dingsi Fang Guan was made Crown Prince Junior Tutor and removed from deliberative posts.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi Fang Guan became crown prince junior tutor and left the council.

sentences.zh: 以諫議大夫張鎬為中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Remonstrance Grandee Zhang Gao was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and concurrent Secretariat-Chancellery Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gao became vice director of the secretariat and grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 以武部侍郎杜鴻漸為河西節度。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of War Du Hongjian was made Hexi military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Du Hongjian became Hexi commissioner.

sentences.zh: 庚申，誥追贈故妃楊氏為元獻皇太后，上母也。

translations.literal: On gengshen a proclamation posthumously invested the late consort Yang as Empress Yuanxian, the emperor's mother.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen his mother, the late Consort Yang, was posthumously made Empress Yuanxian.

sentences.zh: 甲子，郭子儀以失律讓司空，許之。

translations.literal: On jiazi Guo Ziyi, for military fault, yielded the post of Minister of Works and was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi Guo Ziyi resigned the ministry of works for military fault and was allowed.

sentences.zh: 七月庚戌夜，蜀郡軍人郭千仞謀逆，上皇御玄英樓，節度使李峘討平之。

translations.literal: On gengxu night in Shu commandery soldier Guo Qianren plotted treason; the Retired Emperor mounted the Xuanying Tower; military commissioner Li Xian suppressed it.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu night Guo Qianren of Shu plotted treason; Xuanzong took the Xuanying Tower while Li Xian put it down.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，賊將安武臣陷陜郡，民無遺類。

translations.literal: On dingsi the rebel general An Wuchen took Shan commandery; not a person was left.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi An Wuchen took Shan commandery and left no survivor.

sentences.zh: 八月甲申，以黃門侍郎崔渙為餘杭太守、江東採訪防禦使。

translations.literal: On jiashen Vice Director of the Chancellery Cui Huan was made Yuhang prefect and Jiangdong pacification and defense commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen Cui Huan became Yuhang prefect and Jiangdong commissioner.

sentences.zh: 己丑，以平章事張鎬兼河南節度、採訪處置等使。

translations.literal: On jichou Grand Councilor Zhang Gao was made concurrent Henan military commissioner and pacification and disposition commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou Zhang Gao became Henan commissioner with full disposition powers.

sentences.zh: 靈昌太守許叔冀為賊所攻，援兵不至，拔眾投睢陽郡。

translations.literal: Lingchang prefect Xu Shuji was attacked by rebels; relief did not arrive; he led his host to join Suiyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shuji of Lingchang, besieged without relief, led his troops into Suiyang.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，大閱諸軍，上御城樓以觀之。

translations.literal: On guisi the armies were greatly reviewed; the emperor mounted the city tower to watch.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi he reviewed the armies from the city wall.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，改雍縣為鳳翔縣，陳倉為寶雞縣。

translations.literal: On dingyou Yong county was changed to Fengxiang county and Chencang to Baoji county.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou Yong became Fengxiang county and Chencang Baoji.

sentences.zh: 閏八月辛未，賊將遽寇鳳翔，崔光遠行軍司馬王伯倫、判官李椿率眾捍賊。

translations.literal: In the intercalary eighth month, on xinwei, rebel troops suddenly raided Fengxiang; campaigning marshal Wang Bolun and judge Li Chun of Cui Guangyuan led troops to resist.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary eighth month rebels raided Fengxiang; Wang Bolun and Li Chun drove them off.

sentences.zh: 賊退，乘勝至中渭橋，殺賊守橋眾千人，追擊入苑中。

translations.literal: The rebels retreated; pursuing victory to Zhongwei Bridge they killed a thousand bridge guards and chased into the park.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing, they killed a thousand at Zhongwei Bridge and chased into the imperial park.

sentences.zh: 時賊大軍屯武功，聞之燒營而去。

translations.literal: The rebel great army was camped at Wugong; hearing this they burned their camp and left.
translations.idiomatic: The main rebel force at Wugong burned its camp and fled on hearing the news.

sentences.zh: 伯倫與賊血戰而死，李椿力窮被執，然自是賊不敢西侵。

translations.literal: Bolong died fighting the rebels at close quarters; Li Chun, strength exhausted, was captured—yet from then the rebels dared not invade west.
translations.idiomatic: Bolong died in close fight; Li Chun was taken—but rebels never again raided west.

sentences.zh: 九月丁丑，上黨節度使程千里與賊挑戰，為賊將蔡希德所擒。

translations.literal: On dingchou Shangdang military commissioner Cheng Qianli challenged the rebels and was captured by the rebel general Cai Xide.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou Cheng Qianli of Shangdang was captured by Cai Xide.

sentences.zh: 燉煌王承寀自回紇使還，拜宗正卿；

translations.literal: Prince of Dunhuang Chengbao returned from the Huihe mission and was made Director of the Imperial Clan;
translations.idiomatic: Chengbao returned from Huihe and became director of the imperial clan;

sentences.zh: 納回紇公主為妃，回紇封為葉護，持四節，與回紇葉護太子率兵四千助國討賊。

translations.literal: the Huihe princess was taken as consort; Huihe enfeoffed her Yehu, bearing the four insignia; with the Yehu's crown prince she led four thousand troops to aid the state in punishing rebels.
translations.idiomatic: he married the Huihe princess; the Yehu and his crown prince brought four thousand horsemen to fight the rebels.

sentences.zh: 葉護入見，宴賜加等。

translations.literal: The Yehu entered audience; feasting and rewards were increased.
translations.idiomatic: The Yehu was received at court with lavish feasting.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，元帥廣平王統朔方、安西、回紇、南蠻、大食之眾二十萬，東向討賊。

translations.literal: On dinghai Commander-in-Chief Prince of Guangping led Shuofang, Anxi, Huihe, southern barbarian, and Dashi forces—two hundred thousand—and marched east to punish rebels.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai the Prince of Guangping led two hundred thousand from Shuofang, Anxi, Huihe, Nanman, and Dashi east against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，與賊將安守忠、李歸仁等戰於香積寺西北，賊軍大敗，斬首六萬級，賊帥張通儒棄京城東走。

translations.literal: On renyin he fought the rebel generals An Shouzhong and Li Guiren northwest of Xiangji Temple; the rebel army was greatly defeated, sixty thousand heads cut, rebel commander Zhang Tongru abandoned the capital and fled east.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin he crushed An Shouzhong and Li Guiren at Xiangji Temple, took sixty thousand heads, and Zhang Tongru fled the capital.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，廣平王收西京。

translations.literal: On guimao the Prince of Guangping recovered the western capital.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao the Prince of Guangping entered the western capital.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，捷書至行在，百僚稱賀，即日告捷於蜀。

translations.literal: On jiachen the victory report reached the mobile court; the hundred officials congratulated; that day victory was announced to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen word of victory reached court; the ministers rejoiced and the news was sent to Shu.

sentences.zh: 上皇遣裴冕入京，啟告郊廟社稷。

translations.literal: The Retired Emperor sent Pei Mian into the capital to report to the suburban altars and the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: The retired emperor sent Pei Mian to report at the suburban and state altars.

sentences.zh: 冬十月乙巳朔，以崔光遠為京兆尹。

translations.literal: In the tenth winter month, on yisi new moon, Cui Guangyuan was made metropolitan prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Cui Guangyuan became metropolitan prefect.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「緣京城初收，要安百姓，又灑掃宮闕，奉迎上皇。

translations.literal: An edict said: "As the capital is newly recovered, the people must be settled and the palace swept to welcome the Retired Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "The capital is newly taken; we must settle the people, clean the palace, and welcome the retired emperor.

sentences.zh: 以今月十九日還京，應緣供頓，務從減省。

translations.literal: On the nineteenth of this month we return to the capital; all supplies for the journey shall be kept spare."
translations.idiomatic: We return on the nineteenth; keep the journey spare."

sentences.zh: 」吐蕃寇陷西平郡。

translations.literal: Tibet raided and took Xiping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet took Xiping commandery.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，賊將尹子奇陷睢陽，害張巡、姚訚、許遠。

translations.literal: On guichou the rebel general Yin Ziqi took Suiyang and killed Zhang Xun, Yao Yan, and Xu Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou Yin Ziqi took Suiyang and killed Zhang Xun, Yao Yan, and Xu Yuan.

sentences.zh: 賊自香積之敗，悉眾保陜郡，廣平王統郭子儀等進攻，與賊戰於陜西之新店，賊眾大敗，斬首十萬級，橫尸三十里。

translations.literal: After defeat at Xiangji the rebels gathered all their forces to hold Shan commandery; the Prince of Guangping with Guo Ziyi and others advanced to attack and fought at Xindian west of Shan; the rebel host was greatly defeated, one hundred thousand heads cut, corpses lay thirty li.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels massed at Shan; the Prince of Guangping and Guo Ziyi crushed them at Xindian, taking one hundred thousand heads over thirty li.

sentences.zh: 庚申，安慶緒與其黨奔河北。

translations.literal: On gengshen An Qingxu fled north to Hebei with his faction.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen An Qingxu fled to Hebei with his followers.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，廣平王入東京，陳兵天津橋南，士庶歡呼路側。

translations.literal: On renxu the Prince of Guangping entered the eastern capital; troops were arrayed south of Tianjin Bridge and the people cheered along the road.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu the Prince of Guangping entered Luoyang; troops lined Tianjin Bridge as the people cheered.

sentences.zh: 陷賊官偽署侍中陳希烈、中書令張垍等三百餘人素服待罪。

translations.literal: More than three hundred officials who had served the rebels in false posts, including Acting Palace Attendant Chen Xilie and Secretariat Director Zhang Tan, waited in plain clothes for judgment.
translations.idiomatic: More than three hundred collaborators, including Chen Xilie and Zhang Tan, waited in plain clothes for judgment.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，上自鳳翔還京，仍遣太子太師韋見素入蜀迎上皇，鳳翔郡給復五載。

translations.literal: On guihai the emperor returned to the capital from Fengxiang and sent Crown Prince Grand Tutor Wei Jiansu into Shu to welcome the Retired Emperor; Fengxiang commandery was given tax relief for five years.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai he returned from Fengxiang and sent Wei Jiansu to Shu; Fengxiang received five years' tax relief.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，至望賢宮，得東京捷書至，上大喜。

translations.literal: On bingyin he reached Wangxian Palace; the eastern capital victory report arrived and the emperor rejoiced greatly.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin at Wangxian Palace he received word of Luoyang's recovery and rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，入長安。

translations.literal: On dingmao he entered Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao he entered the capital.

sentences.zh: 士庶涕泣拜忭曰：「不圖復見吾君！

translations.literal: The people wept and bowed in joy, saying: "We never thought to see our lord again!
translations.idiomatic: The people wept and bowed: "We never thought to see you again!

sentences.zh: 」上亦為之感惻。

translations.literal: " The emperor also was moved to compassion.
translations.idiomatic: He too was moved to tears.

sentences.zh: 九廟為賊所焚，上素服哭於廟三日，入居大明宮。

translations.literal: The nine temples had been burned by rebels; the emperor wore plain clothes and wept at the temples three days, then moved into the Great Bright Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The ancestral temples had been burned; he mourned in plain dress three days, then entered the Great Bright Palace.

sentences.zh: 是日，上皇發蜀郡。

translations.literal: That day the Retired Emperor departed Shu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: That day the retired emperor left Shu.

sentences.zh: 己巳，文武脅從官免冠徒跣，朝堂待罪，禁之府獄，命中丞崔器劾之。

translations.literal: On jisi civil and military officials who had been coerced removed caps and went barefoot to the court hall to await punishment; they were confined in government prisons and ordered investigated by Censor-in-Chief Cui Qi.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi coerced officials came barefoot to await judgment; Cui Qi was ordered to investigate.

sentences.zh: 回紇葉護自東京還，宴之於宣政殿，便辭還蕃。

translations.literal: The Huihe Yehu returned from the eastern capital; he was feasted in the Xuanzheng Hall and took leave to return to his realm.
translations.idiomatic: The Huihe Yehu was feasted in the Xuanzheng Hall and took leave for home.

sentences.zh: 乃封葉護為忠義王，約每年送絹二萬疋，至朔方王便交授。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed King of Loyal Righteousness, with an agreement to deliver twenty thousand bolts of silk each year, handed over at Shuofang when the king's envoy came.
translations.idiomatic: He was made King of Loyal Righteousness, promised twenty thousand bolts of silk yearly at Shuofang.

sentences.zh: 十一月壬申朔，上御丹鳳樓，下制曰：「我國家出震乘乾，立極開統。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on renshen new moon, the emperor mounted Danfeng Tower and issued an edict: "Our state arose from the thunder trigram, established the pole and opened the succession.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he mounted Danfeng Tower and proclaimed: "Our house arose in thunder, set the pole, and opened a new age.

sentences.zh: 謳歌歷數，啟聖千齡；

translations.literal: Songs of praise and the turn of fate opened a sagely reign of a thousand ages;
translations.idiomatic: Songs of praise opened a sagely thousand-year reign;

sentences.zh: 文物聲名，握圖六葉。

translations.literal: culture and fame, grasping the chart through six generations.
translations.idiomatic: Culture and fame held the mandate through six generations.

sentences.zh: 安祿山夷羯賤類，粗立邊功，遂肆兇殘，變起倉卒，而毒流四海，塗炭萬靈。

translations.literal: An Lushan, a base man of Yi and Jie stock, won slight frontier merit, then let loose cruelty; rebellion rose in haste and poison flowed to the four seas, charring ten thousand souls.
translations.idiomatic: An Lushan, a base frontier soldier, turned cruel; rebellion charred the realm.

sentences.zh: 朕興言痛憤，，提戈問罪，靈武聚一旅之眾，至鳳翔合百萬之師，親總元戎，掃清群孽。

translations.literal: I speak with grief and rage and take up arms to ask justice; at Lingwu I gathered a single brigade, at Fengxiang united a million soldiers, personally commanding the host to sweep away the evil.
translations.idiomatic: I took up arms in grief; at Lingwu I gathered a brigade, at Fengxiang a million men, and led them myself against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 廣平王俶受委元帥，能振天聲；

translations.literal: The Prince of Guangping received the commander's seal and could shake heaven's sound;
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Guangping commanded the armies and shook heaven;

sentences.zh: 郭子儀決勝無前，克成大業。

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi was decisive and unmatched, accomplishing the great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi was unmatched and finished the war.

sentences.zh: 兼回紇葉護、雲南子弟、諸蕃兵馬，力戰平兇，勢若摧枯，易同破竹。

translations.literal: Together with the Huihe Yehu, Yunnan youths, and the armies of the various barbarians, they fought hard to pacify the evil; their force was like snapping dry wood, easy as splitting bamboo.
translations.idiomatic: With the Huihe Yehu, Yunnan troops, and allied barbarians they broke the rebels like dry wood.

sentences.zh: 朕早承聖訓，嘗讀禮經，義切奉先，恐不克荷。

translations.literal: I early received sage instruction and have read the Book of Rites; duty to the ancestors cuts deep, and I feared I could not bear the weight.
translations.idiomatic: I was taught the rites of filial piety and feared I could not bear the ancestral charge.

sentences.zh: 今復宗廟於函洛，迎上皇於巴蜀；

translations.literal: Now the ancestral temples are restored in Hangu and Luo; the Retired Emperor is welcomed from Ba-Shu;
translations.idiomatic: Now the temples stand again in the two capitals and the retired emperor returns from Shu;

sentences.zh: 導鑾輿而反正，朝寢門而問安；

translations.literal: the imperial carriage turns homeward and the sleeping gate is asked after in peace;
translations.idiomatic: the imperial carriage returns and the inner gate knows peace again;

sentences.zh: 寰宇載寧，朕願畢矣。

translations.literal: The realm is at peace; my wish is fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: The realm is whole—my work is done.

sentences.zh: 且復人將有主，敬當天地之心；

translations.literal: Moreover, the people will again have a lord; one must reverently accord with the mind of Heaven and Earth;
translations.idiomatic: The people will again have their rightful ruler; I must honor the will of Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 興豈在予，實憑社稷之祐。

translations.literal: Can renewal rest on me alone? It truly depends on the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: This restoration is not mine to claim—it rests on the blessing of the altars.

sentences.zh: 今兩京無虞，三靈通慶，可以昭事，宜在覃恩，待上皇到日，當取處分。

translations.literal: Now the Two Capitals are secure and the Three Powers rejoice together; we may proclaim the rites and extend grace—when the Retired Emperor arrives, decisions shall be taken then.
translations.idiomatic: The Two Capitals are safe, the Three Powers united in celebration; the time has come to proclaim the rites and grant amnesty—but final disposition awaits the Retired Emperor's return.

sentences.zh: 」是時河南、河東諸郡縣皆平。

translations.literal: 」At that time the commanderies and counties of Henan and Hedong were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: [Close of edict.] By then every commandery and county in Henan and Hedong had been pacified.

sentences.zh: 宮省門帶「安」字者改之。

translations.literal: Palace and ministry gates bearing the character an were renamed.
translations.idiomatic: Every palace and ministry gate whose name contained the character an was changed.

sentences.zh: 偽御史大夫嚴莊來降。

translations.literal: The rebel grand censor Yan Zhuang came over in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhuang, the rebels' grand censor, surrendered.

sentences.zh: 新成九廟神主，上親告享。

translations.literal: The new Nine Ancestral Temple spirit tablets were completed, and the emperor personally performed the announcement rites.
translations.idiomatic: With the new Nine Ancestral Temple spirit tablets ready, the emperor offered the announcement sacrifice in person.

sentences.zh: 十二月丙午，上皇至自蜀，上至望賢宮奉迎。

translations.literal: On bingwu of the twelfth month the Retired Emperor arrived from Shu; the emperor went to Wangxian Palace to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu of the twelfth month the Retired Emperor returned from Shu; the emperor rode to Wangxian Palace to receive him.

sentences.zh: 上皇御宮南樓，上望樓闢易，下馬趨進樓前，再拜蹈舞稱慶。

translations.literal: The Retired Emperor took the south tower of the palace; the emperor looked up at the tower, dismounted, and hurried to the foot of the tower, bowing twice, treading the dance of joy, and voicing congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: The Retired Emperor stood on the palace's south tower; the emperor gazed up, dismounted, ran to the tower's base, bowed twice, danced the congratulatory tread, and cried his felicitations.

sentences.zh: 上皇下樓，上匍匐捧上皇足，涕泗嗚咽，不能自勝。

translations.literal: The Retired Emperor came down from the tower; the emperor crawled forward, held the Retired Emperor's feet in both hands, and wept aloud, unable to master himself.
translations.idiomatic: When the Retired Emperor descended, the emperor prostrated himself, clasped his feet, and sobbed until he could no longer speak.

sentences.zh: 遂扶侍上皇御殿，親自進食；

translations.literal: He then supported the Retired Emperor into the hall and personally served his meal;
translations.idiomatic: He helped the Retired Emperor to the throne hall and served the meal himself;

sentences.zh: 自御馬以進，上皇上馬，又躬攬轡而行，止之後退。

translations.literal: he led his own horse forward; when the Retired Emperor mounted, he again took the reins in hand and walked beside the horse, only withdrawing after being stopped.
translations.idiomatic: then brought his own horse forward; when the Retired Emperor mounted, he walked the horse by the reins and would not step back until repeatedly urged.

sentences.zh: 上皇曰：「吾享國長久，吾不知貴，見吾子為天子，吾知貴矣。

translations.literal: The Retired Emperor said: "I have long enjoyed the realm; I did not know what honor was—now that I see my son emperor, I know honor."
translations.idiomatic: The Retired Emperor said, "I held the realm so long I never knew what glory meant—only now, seeing my son on the throne, do I understand it."

sentences.zh: 」上乘馬前導，自開遠門至丹鳳門，旗幟燭天，彩棚夾道。

translations.literal: 」The emperor rode ahead as guide; from Kaiyuan Gate to Danfeng Gate, banners filled the sky and painted canopies lined the road.
translations.idiomatic: [Close of speech.] The emperor rode in the lead from Kaiyuan Gate to Danfeng Gate, banners blotting out the sky and colored awnings lining the way.

sentences.zh: 士庶舞忭路側，皆曰：「不圖今日再見二聖！

translations.literal: Commoners danced in delight beside the road, all saying: "We never dreamed we would again see the Two Sages!"
translations.idiomatic: People danced along the roadside, crying, "We never thought to live to see both emperors again!"

sentences.zh: 」百僚班於含元殿庭，上皇御殿，左相苗晉卿率百闢稱賀，人人無不感咽。

translations.literal: 」The host of officials formed ranks in the courtyard of Hanyuan Hall; the Retired Emperor took the hall, and left minister Miao Jinqing led the hundred officials in congratulation—every man wept.
translations.idiomatic: [Close of exclamation.] Officials lined the Hanyuan Hall courtyard; the Retired Emperor took the throne, and Miao Jinqing led the hundred officials in felicitation until none could hold back tears.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，上皇詣長樂殿謁九廟神主，即日幸興慶宮。

translations.literal: When the rites were finished, the Retired Emperor went to Changle Hall to visit the Nine Ancestral Temple spirit tablets, and that same day visited Xingqing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: After the ceremony the Retired Emperor visited the Nine Ancestral Temple tablets at Changle Hall and went that day to Xingqing Palace.

sentences.zh: 上請歸東宮，上皇遣高力士再三尉譬而止。

translations.literal: The emperor asked to return to the Eastern Palace; the Retired Emperor sent Gao Lishi again and again to comfort and dissuade him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked to withdraw to the Eastern Palace; the Retired Emperor sent Gao Lishi repeatedly to soothe and stay him.

sentences.zh: 受賊偽署左相陳希烈、達奚珣等二百餘人並禁於楊國忠宅鞫問。

translations.literal: More than two hundred who had accepted rebel appointments—including left minister Chen Xilie and Daxi Xun—were confined in Yang Guozhong's house for interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: Over two hundred men who had served under the rebels—including Chen Xilie, Daxi Xun, and others—were held at Yang Guozhong's residence for questioning.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，以左相苗晉卿為中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: On jiayin, left minister Miao Jinqing was made vice director of the Secretariat and associate director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin Miao Jinqing, left minister, was appointed vice director of the Secretariat and associate director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 十二月戊午朔，上御丹鳳門，下制大赦。

translations.literal: On the wuwu new moon of the twelfth month the emperor took Danfeng Gate and issued a great amnesty edict.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuwu new moon of the twelfth month the emperor appeared at Danfeng Gate and proclaimed a great amnesty.

sentences.zh: 蜀郡靈武元從功臣太子太師、豳國公韋見素，內侍、齊國公高力士，右龍武大將軍陳玄禮，各加實封三百戶。

translations.literal: Meritorious followers from Shu and Lingwu—Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and Duke of Bin Wei Jiansu, chief eunuch and Duke of Qi Gao Lishi, and Right Dragon Martial Grand General Chen Xuanli—each received three hundred households added to their substantive fiefs.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Jiansu, grand preceptor of the heir apparent and Duke of Bin; Gao Lishi, chief eunuch and Duke of Qi; and Chen Xuanli, right dragon martial grand general—all early followers from Shu and Lingwu—each gained three hundred households on their fiefs.

sentences.zh: 田長文、張崇俊、杜休祥各加二百戶。

translations.literal: Tian Changwen, Zhang Chongjun, and Du Xiuxiang each received two hundred households added.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Changwen, Zhang Chongjun, and Du Xiuxiang each received two hundred additional fief households.

sentences.zh: 右僕射裴冕冀國公，殿中監李輔國成國公，宗正卿李遵鄭國公，兼進封邑。

translations.literal: Right vice director Pei Mian was made Duke of Ji; palace director Li Fuguo Duke of Cheng; director of the imperial clan Li Zun Duke of Zheng—each also received enlarged fiefs.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Mian, right vice director, became Duke of Ji; Li Fuguo, palace director, Duke of Cheng; Li Zun, director of the imperial clan, Duke of Zheng—all with enlarged fiefs.

sentences.zh: 廣平王俶封楚王，加實封二千戶。

translations.literal: Prince of Guangping Li Chu was created Prince of Chu, with two thousand households added to his substantive fief.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chu, Prince of Guangping, was created Prince of Chu and granted two thousand additional fief households.

sentences.zh: 左僕射、朔方節度郭子儀加司徒，進封代國公，實封一千戶。

translations.literal: Left vice director and Shuofang military commissioner Guo Ziyi was promoted to grand steward and created Duke of Dai, with a substantive fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi, left vice director and Shuofang commissioner, was made grand steward and Duke of Dai with a thousand-household fief.

sentences.zh: 兵馬使僕固懷恩封豐國公，右金吾將軍李嗣業封虢國公，司徒兼太原尹李光弼薊國公，關內節度王思禮霍國公，淮南節度來瑱潁國公，南陽太守魯炅岐國公，仍並加實封。

translations.literal: Army commissioner Pugu Huai'en was created Duke of Feng; Right Golden Guard General Li Siye Duke of Guo; Grand Steward and concurrent Taiyuan intendant Li Guangbi Duke of Ji; Guannei commissioner Wang Sili Duke of Huo; Huainan commissioner Lai Tian Duke of Ying; Nanyang grand protector Lu Qiong Duke of Qi—all also received added substantive fiefs.
translations.idiomatic: Pugu Huai'en became Duke of Feng; Li Siye, right golden guard general, Duke of Guo; Li Guangbi, grand steward and Taiyuan intendant, Duke of Ji; Wang Sili, Guannei commissioner, Duke of Huo; Lai Tian, Huainan commissioner, Duke of Ying; Lu Qiong, Nanyang grand protector, Duke of Qi—all with enlarged fiefs.

sentences.zh: 京兆尹崔光遠鄴國公，開府李光進范陽郡公，左相苗晉卿為侍中、封韓國公，憲部尚書、平章事李麟褒國公，中書侍郎崔圓為中書令、趙國公，中書侍郎張鎬南陽縣公。

translations.literal: Capital intendant Cui Guangyuan Duke of Ye; Kai fu Li Guangjin Marquis of Fanyang; left minister Miao Jinqing made chief minister and Duke of Han; Minister of Justice and associate director Li Lin Duke of Bao; vice director of the Secretariat Cui Yuan made director of the Secretariat and Duke of Zhao; vice director Zhang Hao Marquis of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Guangyuan, capital intendant, became Duke of Ye; Li Guangjin, kai fu, Marquis of Fanyang; Miao Jinqing, left minister, chief minister and Duke of Han; Li Lin, minister of justice and associate director, Duke of Bao; Cui Yuan, vice director, director of the Secretariat and Duke of Zhao; Zhang Hao, Marquis of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 近日所改百司額及郡名官名，一依故事。

translations.literal: Recent changes to the titles of the hundred offices and to commandery and official names were all restored to the old forms.
translations.idiomatic: Every recent change to office titles, commandery names, and official designations was reversed to the former usage.

sentences.zh: 改蜀郡為南京，鳳翔府為西京，西京改為中京，蜀郡改為成都府。

translations.literal: Shu commandery was renamed Southern Capital; Fengxiang Prefecture Western Capital; the Western Capital became Middle Capital; Shu commandery became Chengdu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shu commandery became the Southern Capital; Fengxiang Prefecture the Western Capital; the old Western Capital the Middle Capital; and Shu commandery Chengdu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 鳳翔府官僚並同三京名號。

translations.literal: Fengxiang officials were given titles matching those of the Three Capitals.
translations.idiomatic: Officials at Fengxiang received ranks parallel to those of the Three Capitals.

sentences.zh: 其李憕、盧弈、顏杲卿、袁履謙、許遠、張巡、張介然、蔣清、龐堅等即與追贈，訪其子孫，厚其官爵。

translations.literal: Li Cheng, Lu Yi, Yan Gaoqing, Yuan Lüqian, Xu Yuan, Zhang Xun, Zhang Jieran, Jiang Qing, Pang Jian, and the like were posthumously ennobled at once; their descendants were sought out and given generous ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cheng, Lu Yi, Yan Gaoqing, Yuan Lüqian, Xu Yuan, Zhang Xun, Zhang Jieran, Jiang Qing, Pang Jian, and others were posthumously honored; their descendants were found and richly rewarded with office.

sentences.zh: 文武三品已上賜爵一級，四品已下加一階。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials of third rank and above were granted one noble rank; those of fourth rank and below received one step of promotion.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of third rank and above gained one noble rank; those of fourth rank and below, one promotion.

sentences.zh: 賜酺五日。

translations.literal: Five days of public feasting were granted.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted five days of public revelry.

sentences.zh: 進封南陽王系為趙王，新城王僅為彭王，潁川王僴為兗王。

translations.literal: Prince of Nanyang Li Xi was advanced to Prince of Zhao; Prince of Xincheng Li Jin to Prince of Peng; Prince of Yingchuan Li Tan to Prince of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xi, Prince of Nanyang, became Prince of Zhao; Li Jin, Prince of Xincheng, Prince of Peng; Li Tan, Prince of Yingchuan, Prince of Yan.

sentences.zh: 第七男侹為涇王，第九男僙封襄王，第十男佋封興王，第十一男倕封杞王，第十二男侗封定王。

translations.literal: The seventh son Ting was made Prince of Jing; the ninth son Huang Prince of Xiang; the tenth son Zhao Prince of Xing; the eleventh son Chui Prince of Qi; the twelfth son Tong Prince of Ding.
translations.idiomatic: The seventh son, Ting, was made Prince of Jing; the ninth, Huang, Prince of Xiang; the tenth, Zhao, Prince of Xing; the eleventh, Chui, Prince of Qi; the twelfth, Tong, Prince of Ding.

sentences.zh: 甲子，上皇御宣政殿，授上傳國璽，上於殿下涕泣而受之。

translations.literal: On jiazi the Retired Emperor took Xuanzheng Hall and handed the emperor the seal of transmission; the emperor received it below the hall steps, weeping.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi the Retired Emperor sat in Xuanzheng Hall and passed down the imperial seal; the emperor accepted it at the foot of the steps in tears.

sentences.zh: 己丑，賊將偽范陽節度使史思明以其兵眾八萬之籍，與偽河東節度使高秀巖並表送降。

translations.literal: On jichou the rebel general and false Fanyang military commissioner Shi Siming, with registers of his eighty thousand troops, and the false Hedong commissioner Gao Xiuyan jointly submitted memorials of surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou Shi Siming, the rebels' Fanyang commissioner, submitted rolls listing eighty thousand men, and Gao Xiuyan, false Hedong commissioner, joined him in surrender.

sentences.zh: 庚午，制：「人臣之節，有死無二；

translations.literal: On gengwu an edict said: "The minister's integrity admits only death, never two masters;
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu an edict declared: "A loyal minister serves one master unto death;

sentences.zh: 為國之體，叛而必誅。

translations.literal: the body politic treats rebellion as warrant for execution.
translations.idiomatic: the state knows no mercy for traitors.

sentences.zh: 況乎委質賊廷，宴安逆命，耽受寵祿，淹延歲時，不顧思義，助其效用，此其可宥，法將何施？

translations.literal: How much more those who pledged themselves to the rebel court, rested at ease in treason, lingered in office enjoying favor year after year, heedless of righteousness, and lent their strength to the enemy—if such men may be spared, what use is the law?
translations.idiomatic: How much worse those who bowed to the rebel court, fattened on treason's favor, and year after year served the enemy—if they may live, what force has law?

sentences.zh: 達奚珣等或受任臺輔，位極人臣；

translations.literal: Daxi Xun and others had held posts at the highest councils, standing at the summit of subjecthood;
translations.idiomatic: Daxi Xun and his like sat in the highest councils, at the very peak of office;

sentences.zh: 或累葉寵榮，姻聯戚里；

translations.literal: some had known favor through generations, linked by marriage to the imperial kin;
translations.idiomatic: some were heirs to generations of grace, bound to the throne by marriage;

sentences.zh: 或歷踐臺閣，或職通中外。

translations.literal: some had risen through the secretariat, or held posts reaching inside and outside the court.
translations.idiomatic: some had climbed the secretariat ladder or held posts that bridged palace and realm.

sentences.zh: 夫以犬馬微賤之畜，猶知戀主；

translations.literal: Even dogs and horses, the meanest of beasts, know devotion to their master;
translations.idiomatic: Even dogs and horses, meanest of creatures, know their master;

sentences.zh: 龜蛇蠢動之類，皆能報恩。

translations.literal: turtles and serpents, creatures of dull motion, can repay a kindness.
translations.idiomatic: turtles and serpents, low and crawling, can repay a debt.

sentences.zh: 豈曰人臣，曾無感激？

translations.literal: Can it be said of human ministers that none felt gratitude?
translations.idiomatic: Are human ministers alone devoid of gratitude?

sentences.zh: 自逆胡作亂，傾覆邦家，凡在黎元，皆含怨憤，殺身殉國者，不可勝數。

translations.literal: Since the rebel barbarian raised chaos and overturned the realm, every commoner has nursed wrath; those who gave their lives for the state are beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Since the rebel scourge overturned the realm, every subject has burned with outrage; the dead who gave their lives for the state cannot be numbered.

sentences.zh: 此等黔首，猶不背國恩。

translations.literal: Even such common folk did not betray the state's grace.
translations.idiomatic: Even the humblest folk did not turn against the throne.

sentences.zh: 受任於梟獍之間，咨謀於豺虺之輩，靜言此情，何可放宥。

translations.literal: Yet these took office among owls and jackals, plotted with wolves and vipers—speaking plainly of such hearts, how can pardon be granted?
translations.idiomatic: Yet these took counsel among owls and jackals, plotted with wolves and vipers—how can such hearts be spared?

sentences.zh: 達奚珣等一十八人，並宜處斬；

translations.literal: The eighteen including Daxi Xun should all be executed;
translations.idiomatic: Daxi Xun and seventeen others shall be executed;

sentences.zh: 陳希烈等七人，並賜自盡；

translations.literal: the seven including Chen Xilie should all be granted self-destruction;
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xilie and six others shall be permitted to take their own lives;

sentences.zh: 前大理卿張均特宜免死，配流合浦郡。

translations.literal: former grand judge of the Court of Judicial Review Zhang Jun is specially to be spared death and exiled to Hepu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun, former grand judge of the Court of Judicial Review, alone shall be spared and exiled to Hepu commandery.

sentences.zh: 」是日斬達奚珣等於子城西南隅獨柳樹，仍集百僚往觀之。

translations.literal: 」That day Daxi Xun and the others were beheaded at the Lone Willow south of the inner city's southwest corner, and the hundred officials were assembled to witness it.
translations.idiomatic: [Close of edict.] That day Daxi Xun and the rest were beheaded at the Lone Willow Tree southwest of the inner city, with the hundred officials summoned to watch.

sentences.zh: 乾元元年三載正月甲戌朔。

translations.literal: On the jiaxu new moon, first month of the third year of Qianyuan.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiaxu new moon of the first month of Qianyuan 1.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，上皇御宣政殿，冊皇帝尊號曰光天文武大聖孝感皇帝。

translations.literal: On wuyin the Retired Emperor took Xuanzheng Hall and invested the emperor with the honorific title Luminous Heaven, Cultured in War, Great Sage, Filially Attentive Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin the Retired Emperor sat in Xuanzheng Hall and bestowed the honorific Luminous Heaven, Cultured in War, Great Sage, Filially Attentive Emperor.

sentences.zh: 上以徽號中有「大聖」二字，上表固讓，不允。

translations.literal: Because the honorific contained the two characters "Great Sage," the emperor memorialized firmly declining; permission was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor petitioned to decline the words Great Sage in the title; the court would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，敕：「因亂所失庫物，先差使搜檢，如聞下吏因便擾人，其搜檢使一切並停，務令安輯。

translations.literal: On yiyou an edict said: "Treasury goods lost in the chaos were first sent out for search and recovery; it is heard that subordinate officials use the occasion to harass the people—the search commissioners are all halted at once; let calm and order be the aim."
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou an edict read: "Goods lost in the rebellion were to be recovered by search commissioners—but subordinates use the task to prey on the people. All such commissioners are halted; let order be restored."

sentences.zh: 」內出宮女三千人。

translations.literal: Three thousand palace women were released from within.
translations.idiomatic: Three thousand palace women were released from the inner quarters.
