translations.literal: 【Historian’s appraisal】 The historian says: Whenever I read the Odes and reach Lady Xu Mu hearing of her state’s overthrow, or the Zhou grandees grieving millet over ruined halls—their words troubled and earnest, their remonstrance painstaking—I always lay down the book and sigh.
translations.idiomatic: 【Historian’s appraisal】 The historian writes: Reading the Odes to Lady Xu Mu’s grief for a fallen state, or Zhou nobles mourning millet among ruins—I always close the book and sigh.

sentences.zh: 及觀天寶失馭，流離奔播，又甚於詩人之於邑也。

translations.literal: When I behold the loss of reins in the Tianbao era, flight and exile, it exceeds even the poets’ distress.
translations.idiomatic: The Tianbao collapse and flight surpassed even those poets’ sorrow.

sentences.zh: 當其戎羯負恩，奄為豨突，豺豕遽興於轂下，胡越寧慮於舟中，借人之戈，持之反刺，變生於不意也。

translations.literal: When the Rong and Jie broke faith and surged like boars, jackals rose beneath the chariot wheels and barbarians from north and south crowded the boats—borrowing another’s spear to turn it back, disaster came unlooked-for.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarians broke faith; beasts swarmed the capital; north and south filled the boats—spears borrowed were turned inward, and ruin came unawares.

sentences.zh: 所幸太王去國，豳人不忘於周君；

translations.literal: Yet when Great King went from his land, the Bin people did not forget their Zhou lord;
translations.idiomatic: Yet when Great King left Bin, the people still loved their Zhou lord;

sentences.zh: 新莽據圖，黔首仍思於漢德。

translations.literal: when Xin Mang seized the mandate, common folk still yearned for Han virtue.
translations.idiomatic: when Xin Mang took the throne, the people still longed for Han.

sentences.zh: 是以宣皇帝蒙六聖之遺業，因百姓之樂推。

translations.literal: Thus the Manifest Filial Emperor inherited the legacy of six sages and rode the people’s acclaim.
translations.idiomatic: So Suzong took six sages’ legacy and the people’s acclaim.

sentences.zh: 號令朔方，旬日而車徒雲合；

translations.literal: Proclaiming command from Shuofang, in ten days chariots and foot gathered like clouds;
translations.idiomatic: From Shuofang his call ran; in ten days armies clouded the horizon;

sentences.zh: 旋師右輔，期月而關、隴砥平。

translations.literal: turning the army to the right capital, within a month Pass and Longxi were made level.
translations.idiomatic: wheeling to the western capital, within a month Pass and Longxi lay level.

sentences.zh: 故兩都再復於鑾輿，九廟復歆於黍稷。

translations.literal: So the two capitals welcomed the imperial carriage again, and the nine temples once more received millet offerings.
translations.idiomatic: The two capitals took back the throne; the nine temples tasted millet again.

sentences.zh: 觀其迎上皇於蜀道，陳拜慶於望賢，父子於是感傷，行路為之隕涕。

translations.literal: See how he met the retired emperor on the Shu road and offered celebration at Wangxian: father and son wept, and passersby shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: He met his father on the Shu road and bowed at Wangxian—father, son, and every passerby wept.

sentences.zh: 昔太公迎子，或從家令之言；

translations.literal: Of old, Taigong welcomed his son, perhaps following the house steward’s counsel;
translations.idiomatic: Taigong once welcomed a son on a steward’s word;

sentences.zh: 而西伯事親，靡怠寢門之問。

translations.literal: yet Duke of the West served his kin and never slackened the bedchamber door’s inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: yet the Duke of the West never failed the bedchamber door.

sentences.zh: 曾參、孝己，足以擬倫。

translations.literal: Zeng Shen and Xiaoji offer enough parallel.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Shen and Xiaoji are fit comparison.

sentences.zh: 然而道屈知幾，志微遠略。

translations.literal: Yet the Way bent short of knowing the moment; his aims were slight and foresight thin.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he missed the moment; his vision ran short.

sentences.zh: 殘妖未殄，宜先恢復之謀；

translations.literal: Rebel remnants undestroyed, recovery should have come first;
translations.idiomatic: Rebels still lived—recovery should have come first;

sentences.zh: 餘燼才收，何暇升平之禮。

translations.literal: ash barely gathered, what leisure for rites of great peace?
translations.idiomatic: embers still smoked—what time for rites of peace?

sentences.zh: 方聽王璵伏奏，輔國贊成，紺轅躬籍於春郊，翠幰先蠶於繭館、或御殿曉宣時令，或登壇宿禮貴神。

translations.literal: He listened to Wang Yu kneeling in memorial and Li Fuguo urging approval—the dark canopy tilling spring fields, the green carriage leading silkworms at the Cocoon Hall; or holding dawn court to proclaim seasons, or mounting the altar to lodge all night honoring the spirits.
translations.idiomatic: He heard Wang Yu and Li Fuguo urge rites—the emperor plowing spring fields, the empress leading silkworms, dawn audiences for seasons, night vigils at the altars.

sentences.zh: 禮即宜然，時何暇給。

translations.literal: Rites in themselves were fitting; when had time to spare?
translations.idiomatic: The rites were right; the hour was wrong.

sentences.zh: 鐘懸未移於簨虡，思明已陷於洛陽，是知祝史疇人，安能及遠。

translations.literal: Bells had not yet shifted on the bell-frame when Siming already took Luoyang—so much for prayer clerks and calendar officers reaching far ahead.
translations.idiomatic: Bells had not moved when Siming took Luoyang—what prayer clerk sees that far?

sentences.zh: 猶賴大臣宣力，諸將效忠，旄頭終隕於三川，杲日重明於六合。

translations.literal: Yet great ministers bore the burden and generals proved loyal: the Comet Banner fell at last in the Three Rivers, the bright sun shone again over all within the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: Yet ministers and generals endured: the comet fell in the Three Rivers; the sun shone over the realm again.

sentences.zh: 比平王之遷洛，我則英雄；

translations.literal: Compared to King Ping’s move to Luoyang, ours was heroic;
translations.idiomatic: Beside King Ping’s flight to Luoyang, this was heroism;

sentences.zh: 論元帝之渡江，彼誠麼麼。

translations.literal: set beside Emperor Yuan’s crossing the Yangtze, that was petty indeed.
translations.idiomatic: beside Emperor Yuan’s Yangtze crossing, that was small.

sentences.zh: 寧親復國，肅乃休哉！

translations.literal: To comfort kin and restore the realm—Suzong’s was a true rest!
translations.idiomatic: To heal kin and restore the state—Suzong’s rest was real!

sentences.zh: 贊曰：犬羊犯順，輦輅播遷。

translations.literal: 【Eulogy】 The eulogy says: Dogs and sheep rebelled; the imperial carriage wandered.
translations.idiomatic: 【Eulogy】 Dogs and sheep rose; the throne wandered.

sentences.zh: 兇徒竟斃，景祚重延。

translations.literal: The felons died at last; the imperial fortune lengthened again.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels died; the mandate lengthened.

sentences.zh: 星馳蜀道，雨泣望賢。

translations.literal: Stars racing on the Shu road, rain weeping at Wangxian.
translations.idiomatic: Stars flew on the Shu road; rain fell at Wangxian.

sentences.zh: 孝宣之謚，誰曰不然？

translations.literal: The posthumous name Filial and Martial—who says it is not so?
translations.idiomatic: Filial and Martial—who denies the name?
